status_summary: Executive Order 14167 (signed 2025-01-20, published 2025-01-30) directed the Defense Department to submit a Unified Command Plan revision giving U.S. Northern Command the border-sealing mission; a 2025-04-11 presidential memorandum (NSPM-4) then provided for military jurisdiction over southern-border federal lands and the designation of National Defense Areas, and Public Land Order 7963 (effective 2025-04-15) transferred about 109,651 acres in New Mexico to the Army for border security for three years. By 2025-06-11 the Associated Press reported that troops were detaining people accused of trespassing in national defense areas in New Mexico, with a second area in western Texas, and handing them to Border Patrol, and that more than 1,400 people had been charged with entering militarized areas; a New Mexico judge dismissed more than 100 of the national security charges. NSPM-4 preserves authority to request National Guard support for law enforcement under title 32, but the sources do not describe National Guard participation in border arrests.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14167 directed the Secretary of Defense to deliver a Unified Command Plan revision assigning Northern Command a border-sealing mission and to assess options against mass unlawful entry and transnational criminal organizations.

Presidential memorandum NSPM-4 directs transfer of jurisdiction over southern-border federal lands to the Defense Department, provides for designation of National Defense Areas, and preserves authority to request National Guard support under title 32.

Public Land Order 7963 takes effect, transferring about 109,651 acres of federal land in Dona Ana, Luna and Hidalgo Counties, New Mexico, to Army jurisdiction for border security for three years (published 2025-04-21 at 90 FR 16698).

The Associated Press reported that troops had begun detaining people accused of trespassing in national defense areas on the southern border in New Mexico and briefly holding them until Border Patrol took custody.

title: Use military and National Guard personnel in southwest border arrest operations
uncertainties: The Secretary of Defense's own designation of each National Defense Area was not read; the New Mexico area rests on Public Land Order 7963 and an Army article, and the western Texas area rests on the news report. A correction notice listed on the Federal Register public inspection site (filed 2026-03-20) gives a revised acreage of about 110,967 acres for Public Land Order 7963; it was not read in its published form. The AP figures on charges and the New Mexico dismissals were not checked against court records. Developments after June 2025, including later court rulings on the trespass charges and any National Guard arrest role, were not found in a search. NSPM-4 does not itself direct arrests or detentions; the detention practice rests on the AP report and the Army's description. The recommendation sits in the DOJ chapter but is carried out mainly by the Defense and Homeland Security departments.
